title: Explaining Minds and Brains
position: Cross-listed orientation course for Mind, Brain and AI
purpose: A proposed course in the Corniversity catalogue (Cross-listed orientation course for Mind, Brain and AI). Levels of explanation (computational, algorithmic, implementation), normative, descriptive and mechanistic models, representation and computation, prediction versus explanation versus causal evidence, and how a model can be useful without explaining everything.
description: Proposed course: Explaining Minds and Brains. Central question: What counts as an explanation of a mind or brain? centralQuestion: What counts as an explanation of a mind or brain?
prerequisiteGuidance: None beyond careful reading. It is the programme's intellectual foundation, not a motivational introduction, and it is meant to be short so the rest of the programme can begin.
preparationPath: Verified introductions to levels of explanation are on the MBI-01 shelf (Blokpoel and van Rooij, chapter 2; Gershman's draft textbook, chapter 1; the Gureckis course notes 'Minds and Machines'); choose the spine among them, verify two or three worked examples of competing explanations of the same behavioural result, and prepare a first unit around the comparison activity below. The prepared units COG-201 unit 1 (computational-level analysis) and NEU-220 unit 1 (models of what, how and why) already serve part of this ground.
plannedActivities: Two explanations of one behavioural result: state each one's assumptions, the predictions on which they agree, and a condition on which they differ.
Separate what is observed, what a model assumes, what it predicts, and what evidence would challenge it.
